battle.name: 維塔利安的起義
battle.brief: 五一一至五一三年，禁軍護衛官維塔利安率伊利利亞野戰軍奪取波諾尼亞，再沿艾米利亞大道封鎖拉文納，逼皇帝阿納斯塔修斯讓步。卡面這件羅馬弩砲是隨軍行進的扭力投射器，一發一具箭，本該架在營門與陣線後方；拉文納的史料卻沒有留下它涉案的字句。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 這場起義的奇特之處，在於交戰的兩方都是羅馬人。叛方是羅馬帝國駐伊利利亞的野戰軍：維塔利安是軍團級的護衛官兼御前書記（tribunus et notarius），官階不算高，卻握著一支人數可觀的常備兵，以及一批久欠犒賞、紀律廢弛的野戰兵。他在五一二年秋於潘諾尼亞的波諾尼亞（今波隆那）舉兵，得到被免職的潘諾尼亞軍務總監歐多亞塞（Odoacer）與一批不滿現任朝廷的軍官擁護；數月之間，他控制了整個潘諾尼亞與達爾馬提亞，把艾米利亞大道與通往拉文納的北意大利通道握在手中。帝國一方由皇帝阿納斯塔修斯一世坐鎮君士坦丁堡，他自三九五年在位、五〇七年起獨攬大權；朝中樞機多年操在閹人出身的御前總管克律薩菲烏斯手中，這正是維塔利安指名要撤換的人。皇帝先後派出軍務總監馬里努斯與近臣魯菲努斯前往談判，兩人卻在赴約途中被維塔利安的部下所殺，帝國的權威就這樣折在拉文納城外。與此同時，北方森林與草原上的日耳曼諸部趁羅馬內鬥之際湧入：赫魯利人先是支持維塔利安，隨後在布伊里奈人、圖爾文吉人等部落的跟隨下越過多瑙河，進入色雷斯與摩西亞，再順著亞平寧半島的通道打到義大利。從西邊來的是汪達爾控制的北非，其船隊照常把糧食運抵拉文納的克拉塞港，這條海上補給線是帝國能撐住拉文納的唯一依靠。指揮體系上，叛軍以維塔利安一人為核心，加上伊利利亞與潘諾尼亞兩處野戰軍原有的指揮鏈，命令靠軍中口令與旗幟傳遞，實際運作接近軍事獨裁；帝國的野戰軍則按晚期羅馬的標準編制分為步兵大隊（限疆步兵團每團約五百至一千人）、騎兵部隊（輔騎大隊約五百人，重騎大隊約二百五十人）與各式特種兵，攻城與投射器械由軍械官（magister officiorum）掌管，總指揮權先後落在馬里努斯、魯菲努斯與後來的尤提米烏斯、約翰等人手上。軍餉、賞賜與軍糧靠皇室財政與各地物資供應，這條線在起義爆發後被叛軍切斷在義大利中段，成為拉文納守軍最大的困境。
countriesEn: What makes this revolt unusual is that both sides were Romans. The insurgents were the field army of the Roman Empire stationed in Illyricum: Vitalian was a legionary tribune and notarius, an officer of respectable but not especially senior rank, who nonetheless held a substantial body of regular troops and a number of frontier soldiers long overdue their donatives and slack in discipline. In the autumn of 512 he seized Bononia in Pannonia, modern Bologna, and was joined by Odoacer, the dismissed magister militum of the Pannonian command, together with a group of officers alienated by the court in Constantinople; within months he controlled the whole of Pannonia and Dalmatia and held the Via Aemilia and the northern approaches into Italy. The imperial side was Emperor Anastasius I, who sat in Constantinople; he had reigned since 395 and ruled alone since 507, and for years the real machinery of government had been in the hands of Chrysaphius, the eunuch praetorian prefect, precisely the man Vitalian singled out for removal. The emperor sent the magister militum Marinus and the courtier Rufinus to negotiate, and both were killed on the road by Vitalian's men, so that the empire's authority broke in pieces outside Ravenna. At the same time the Germanic peoples of the northern forests and steppes poured in to profit from the Roman civil war: the Heruli first supported Vitalian and then, followed by the Buirinae, the Tervingi and other bands, crossed the Danube into Thrace and Moesia and pushed down the peninsula into Italy. From the west came the Vandal kingdom in North Africa, whose fleets still carried grain to the port of Classe at Ravenna; that maritime supply line was the only thing on which the imperial city could rely. On the command side the rebel army revolved around Vitalian alone, supplemented by the existing chains of command of the Illyrian and Pannonian field armies; orders travelled by word of mouth and by signal inside the camp, and the whole thing operated in effect as a military dictatorship. The imperial field army followed the standard late Roman organisation, with infantry units running from five hundred to a thousand men each, cavalry formations of about five hundred for the auxiliary alae and about two hundred fifty for the heavy alae, and a variety of special troops; the siege and artillery equipment was in the hands of the magister officiorum, and overall command passed in turn to Marinus, Rufinus, and later Euthymius and John. Pay, donatives and grain came from the imperial treasury and from the provinces, and once the rebels cut that line in central Italy the garrison of Ravenna was left in its greatest difficulty.
people: 維塔利安·瓦萊里奧（Marcus Aurelius Valerius Vitalianus）是這場起義的核心人物。他出身並不顯赫，靠軍功升到禁軍級的護衛官，又以書記身分出入御前，頗得士兵之心。他並非單純的權力獵手：軍中傳言他以信奉卡爾西敦公會議為號召，指責皇帝阿納斯塔修斯縱容一性論派、迫害正統信徒，又私下扣下本該分給士兵的賞錢，把怨氣攬到自己身上。五一二年秋，他率部在波諾尼亞奪城，隨即自稱「國家伯爵」（comes rei publicae），又接管色雷斯的軍權，成了實質上的軍區總司令，並要求皇帝撤換克律薩菲烏斯、回到卡爾西敦。皇帝阿納斯塔修斯一世是危機中的另一主角。他出身狄利翁，是帶日耳曼血統的皇帝，在位二十三年，以財政敏銳著稱，也以強行推動一性論化的宗教政策、把關係最壞的閹官留在身邊著稱。五一二年的「阿金狄諾斯事件」把朝野怨氣推到頂點：掌管御內廷的阿金狄諾斯因拒絕交出一筆巨款而被皇帝下令處死，家屬遭清算；事後又有冒名者率眾在跑馬場鬧事，被殺之後追捕同黨，又牽連數百人被處決。這件事之後，軍隊的態度變得危險，而維塔利安正是從軍隊的怨氣裡站出來的人。被派去談判的兩位重臣，軍務總監馬里努斯與近臣魯菲努斯，被殺在赴約途中；此後再沒有一名使者能從維塔利安的營中回來。皇帝最後只剩兩條路：讓步，或者別的辦法。答案是別的辦法——五一五年（部分史家記為五一六年）十二月二十八日，維塔利安在拉文納被自己的姪子殺害，一說此舉由皇帝授意。維塔利安一死，依附他的將領在君士坦丁堡起事，赫魯利人與其他日耳曼部落隨即大舉西進，攻入希臘與小亞細亞，又打到義大利，羅馬人的內戰就此變成外患。東哥特王狄多里克奉皇帝之命出擊支持維塔利安的赫魯利人；維塔利安死後，狄多里克轉而攻取維塔利安黨羽所在的摩西亞與色雷斯，隨後於四九〇年代起兵西征，最終在四九三年除掉汪達爾，成為義大利的實際主人。帝國方面，五一八年在波河平原擊潰入侵者的，是軍務總監尤提米烏斯與卡帕多細亞人約翰率領的野戰軍；卡西奧多魯斯則以軍械官的身分在五一九年前後代表皇帝與赫魯利人談判，用金錢換回被圍的羅馬軍人，隨後寫下《哥特人史》。
peopleEn: Vitalian, Marcus Aurelius Valerius Vitalianus, is the man at the centre of this revolt. He was not of especially distinguished birth, rose on military service to the rank of tribune in the scholae, and through his work as a notarius had access to the imperial presence, which made him popular with the soldiers. He was not simply a man after power: the army said that he raised the banner of Chalcedonian orthodoxy, accused the emperor Anastasius of favouring the Monophysites and of persecuting the orthodox, and held back the donatives due to the men so that the resentment attached to himself. In the autumn of 512 he seized Bononia with his troops, at once styled himself comes rei publicae, took over the command in Thrace, and became in substance a regional commander, and he demanded the removal of Chrysaphius and a return to Chalcedon. Emperor Anastasius I is the other principal figure in the crisis. He came from Dyrrahachium, was an emperor of Germanic blood, and had reigned for twenty-three years, celebrated for financial shrewdness and equally for forcing a Monophysite religious policy on the empire and for keeping the most odious eunuch at court. The Akindynos affair of 512 pushed the resentment of the capital and the army to its height: Akindynos, who ran the imperial household, was executed on the emperor's orders for refusing to hand over a large sum of money, and his family was purged; afterwards an impostor claiming to be Akindynos led a disturbance in the Hippodrome and was killed, and the pursuit of his followers drew in the execution of several hundred men. After that the mood of the troops turned dangerous, and Vitalian was the man who rose out of the army's anger. The two envoys sent to negotiate, the magister militum Marinus and the courtier Rufinus, were killed on the road to their meeting, and after them no messenger ever came back from Vitalian's camp. The emperor was left with two choices: give way, or find another way. He found another way: on 28 December 515, or by some accounts 516, Vitalian was killed at Ravenna by his own nephew, and the story goes that the emperor had sanctioned it. Vitalian's death was followed by a rising of his adherents in Constantinople and by a great westward drive of the Heruli and other Germanic peoples into Greece and Asia Minor and then into Italy, so that a Roman civil war became a foreign invasion. The Ostrogothic king Theodoric was ordered to attack the Heruli who had supported Vitalian; after Vitalian's death Theodoric turned instead upon the partisans of Vitalian in Moesia and Thrace, and then from 490 he moved west, finally destroying Odoacer in 493 and becoming the effective master of Italy. On the imperial side the army that destroyed the invaders in the plain of the Po in 518 was commanded by Euthymius and by John the Cappadocian, and Cassiodorus, as magister officiorum, negotiated with the Heruli around 519 and bought back the Roman soldiers trapped in the siege, before writing his Getica.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是羅馬弩砲（scorpio）：一具扭力弩砲，以青銅或鐵製的機架、兩束絞緊的牛筋或馬腱作扭簧，箭槽上架一具粗重的鐵芯箭，一發一具，靠絞盤與人力拉弦發射。維特魯維烏斯記載的那型「手弩砲」（cheiroballistra）由三人抬行，是羅馬軍中規模最小的投射器；較重的車載弩砲（carroballista）則架在二輪或三輪車上，隨軍行進。就本役而言，可以確定的事實有兩層。第一層是它在體系中的位置：羅馬弩砲從共和末年起一直是軍隊的有機投射兵器，晚期羅馬的野戰軍與禁軍仍保有專職的射手與投射兵器小隊，《職官志》所列的邊疆野戰軍編制裡，弩砲小隊與弓手小隊同步兵、騎兵並列；它隨軍隊行軍，宿營時用來護衛營柵與輜重，野戰時在步兵陣線後方或兩翼發射，用以壓制敵軍密集隊形、遮蔽己方進攻，攻城則用來射擊城頭與攀城者。它不需要多少訓練，這正是它比需要專人操作的巨型發石機更容易留存在野戰部隊中的原因。第二層是這場戰爭本身的空白。五一二至五一五年拉文納外圍的戰事，現存記載主要出自編年史（馬爾凱利努斯·科梅斯、《五一八年編年史》殘卷）、普羅科匹烏斯《戰史》第三卷以及埃瓦格里烏斯的教會史，這些文字提到圍城、斷糧、談判、暗殺，卻幾乎不點兵器的名稱，也沒有任何一場戰鬥提到弩砲。因此「維塔利安以弩砲攻擊拉文納」這類說法並無文獻支持，只能作為同時代軍隊配置的合理推測。可以用來對照的，是二十餘年後普羅科匹烏斯留下的記錄：五三三年貝利撒留進軍義大利時，隨軍有一千具發石機與弩砲，由五百對騾子牽引，另有數百具較輕的投射器與投石槌；六九八年攻迦太基時，羅馬營中約有五百七十具發石機與一百一十五具投石機。這說明晚羅馬的野戰軍並不是沒有投射兵器，而是它們的規模、用途與陣位在編年史裡被省略了。同一時期還可以確定：拉文納守軍靠城牆上架設的固定弩砲與海路補給撐住圍攻，赫魯利人五一七年攻羅馬打的是糧道而不是城牆，帝國的解圍手段主要是談判與金錢，而不是投射兵器對攻。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Roman scorpio, a torsion-powered bolt-thrower: a bronze or iron frame carrying two bundles of tightly twisted sinew torsion springs, a trough laid with a single heavy iron-shanked bolt, fired by a windlass and the pull of the crew. The type described by Vitruvius, the cheiroballistra, could be carried by three men and was the smallest of the Roman missile engines; the heavier carroballista stood on a two- or three-wheeled cart and travelled with the column. As for this campaign, the certain facts come in two layers. The first is the place the weapon held in the system: the Roman bolt-thrower had been an organic arm of the army since the late Republic, and the late Roman field army and the scholae palatinae still maintained specialist missile units, with the ballista and sagittarius squads listed alongside the infantry and cavalry in the field establishment of the Notitia Dignitatum. It marched with the army, was used to defend the camp fence and the baggage at night, and in battle was fired from behind the infantry line or from the flanks to break up enemy formations and cover an advance; in sieges it shot at the walls and at the assaulting columns. It required little training, and that is precisely why it survived in field armies more readily than the great stone-throwing engines that demanded specialist crews. The second layer is the blank in this campaign's record. The fighting around Ravenna from 512 to 515 survives mainly in the chroniclers, Marcellinus Comes, the fragments of the Chronicle of 518, in the third book of Procopius' Wars, and in Evagrius' Ecclesiastical History; these texts speak of siege, of famine, of negotiation and of murder, but they almost never name a weapon, and not one battle mentions a bolt-thrower. Statements to the effect that Vitalian battered Ravenna with scorpions therefore have no documentary support and can only be a reasonable inference from the equipment of a contemporary army. For comparison one may use what Procopius wrote a little more than twenty years later: when Belisarius invaded Italy in 533 he had a thousand mangonels and bolt-throwers drawn by five hundred pairs of mules, together with several hundred lighter missile engines and petraries; in 698, before Carthage, the Roman camp is credited with about five hundred seventy mangonels and a hundred fifteen petraries. The late Roman field army was not without missile artillery, then; it is simply that its scale, its employment and its place in the line were passed over by the chroniclers. Two further things are certain for the same period: the garrison of Ravenna held out on the fixed bolt-throwers mounted on its walls and on seaborne supply, the Herulian assault on Rome in 517 was aimed at the grain road rather than at the walls, and the imperial relief of the city came chiefly through negotiation and money rather than through an artillery duel.
tactics: 維塔利安的起義本身是一場以道路與政治罷工為骨幹的戰役。他奪下波諾尼亞，等於拿住艾米利亞大道的北端與波河下游的徵糧通道；從波隆那到拉文納公路約二百三十公里，叛軍沿大道南下，一路收編沿線城鎮與野戰軍營，把整個北意大利的徵募與稅收切斷。帝國的野戰軍無法從高盧或北非經陸路入援，援兵只能走海路抵克拉塞港再北上，這正是圍城能夠拖下去的原因。拉文納的形勢本身也說明圍城的性質：這座城是海上要塞式的首都，糧食與援軍靠地中海與亞得里亞海的船隊從非洲與東地中海送來，陸路只需封住通往波隆那與里米尼的兩條大道。維塔利安的部署因此是「封陸不攻牆」：以騎兵巡邏截斷北來的援軍與徵糧隊，以步兵與投射兵器封鎖城郊的道路與橋樑，同時用談判為自己爭取時間。帝國使者一到即被殺，說明他早已把表態做成了條件。皇帝退讓後，他於五一三年以凱旋式進入羅馬，接受了執政官（consul）與「國家伯爵」的頭銜，隨後又取得色雷斯軍區的指揮權；這些頭銜換來的是數年之內他可以不經請旨調動色雷斯的兵馬。叛軍在技術層面的另一面是營壘與器械的運用：羅馬軍隊的野戰營是方形的，四角立木柵與拒馬，門前挖壕，營內按建制分帳，兵器與備用彈藥集中在指定位置；攻城與野戰用的弩砲隨行在輜重隊中，宿營時先架在營門與側翼，因為它的任務不是攻拆城池，而是攔截逼近的騎兵與步兵。相對地，赫魯利人西進時幾乎不帶攻城器械，其戰法是快速騎兵突進、包抄與斷糧，而不是圍城。五一八年帝國野戰軍在波河平原擊潰入侵者的一戰，戰術骨架是「以輕裝騎兵誘敵深入，再以主力騎兵與步兵同時出手」：敵軍的戰車與輜重被拉成長列，羅馬騎兵繞到側翼切斷其退路，步兵與投射兵器在正面壓住追兵，潰散的一翼被殲於平原之上。慘敗者中大量是未經訓練、難以約束的日耳曼部眾，羅馬方面的收穫是把俘虜分派到帝國領地上的殖民莊園充作屯墾的勞力。同一批人馬在更早的年份，正是維塔利安用來威脅君士坦丁堡的資本。
tacticsEn: The skeleton of Vitalian's revolt was a campaign fought with roads and a political strike. By seizing Pannonia he had taken the northern end of the Via Aemilia and the channel along which the Po valley was taxed; from Bologna to Ravenna is about two hundred and thirty kilometres by road, and the rebels marched south along it, absorbing the towns and the field camps on the way and cutting off recruitment and taxation across the whole of northern Italy. The imperial field army could not reach Italy by land from Gaul or North Africa; reinforcements had to come by sea to Classe and then move north, and that is why the blockade could be prolonged. The position of Ravenna itself explains the nature of the siege: the city was a capital built like a maritime fortress, fed by fleets bringing grain and men across the Mediterranean and the Adriatic from Africa and the eastern Mediterranean, and on land it was enough to close the two roads to Bononia and to Rimini. Vitalian's arrangement was therefore to seal the land and not to attack the walls: cavalry patrols cut off reinforcements and tax parties coming from the north, infantry and missile troops covered the roads and the bridges outside the city, and negotiation was used to buy time. The imperial envoys were killed the moment they arrived, which shows that he had already turned any statement of terms into a condition. After the emperor gave way he entered Rome in triumph in 513, accepted the consulship and the title of comes rei publicae, and then took the command in Thrace; what those titles bought him was several years in which he could move the Thracian forces without asking leave. The other side of the rebels' technique was the ordering of camp and machine. The Roman field camp was square, with wooden palisades and chevaux-de-frise at the corners, a ditch before the gates, quarters allotted by unit inside, and weapons and spare ammunition collected in designated places; the bolt-throwers used in the field and in siege travelled with the baggage and were set up first at the camp gates and on the flanks, because their task was not to break cities but to intercept approaching horse and foot. By contrast the Heruli who moved west brought almost no siege engines with them: their method was the fast cavalry rush, the encirclement and the cutting of supply, not the siege. In the battle of 518 in which the imperial field army destroyed the invaders in the plain of the Po, the tactical skeleton was to draw the enemy in with light cavalry and then strike with the main body of horse and foot together: the enemy wagon train and battle line were stretched out in a long column, Roman cavalry worked round to the flank to cut the line of retreat, infantry and the missile troops pinned the pursuit in front, and the broken wing was destroyed on the plain. Many of the defeated were Germanic bands untrained and hard to control, and the Roman profit was the assignment of prisoners to colonizing estates on imperial territory to serve as settler labour. The same sort of men, a few years earlier, had been the capital with which Vitalian threatened Constantinople.
data: 先校年：卡面編號所標的五一一年，落在起義常被繫年的五一一至五一二年之交。編年史把維塔利安奪取波諾尼亞記在五一二年，把他進軍拉文納記在五一三年，把皇帝讓步與他取得執政官頭銜記在五一三年末至五一四年初，把他的遇害記在五一五年十二月二十八日（部分史家作五一六年）；維塔利安身後赫魯利人西征義大利，則在五一六至五一八年。本條目把起始年定為五一一，起始月份只能取年初，因為可考的起義徵候是維塔利安在軍中拒發犒賞、招集舊部，而公開奪城要到次年。戰役的地理可以用三個點標定：波隆那（北緯四十四點四九分，東經十一度三四分）、拉文納（北緯四十四點四二分，東經十二度二十分）、羅馬（北緯四十一度五三分，東經十二度三十分）；波隆那至拉文納公路約二百三十公里，羅馬至拉文納約三百公里。人數方面沒有可引用的確數。維塔利安的起義軍由伊利利亞與潘諾尼亞兩處野戰軍拼湊而成，人數當在數千至一萬之間；同期羅馬帝國的野戰軍總量遠大於此，晚期羅馬常備野戰軍在冊約三十個限疆步兵團（各家統計略有出入），每團五百至一千人，加上騎兵與輔助部隊，總數當以數萬計。這說明維塔利安的兵變在規模上不足以與帝國的總體力量對抗，它能成立，靠的是皇帝在東邊、主力兵在西北的時間差。幾組可以引用的旁證數字：阿金狄諾斯事變後被處決者的數目各家記載不一，或云數百人；阿納斯塔修斯在位期間把金幣（solidus）的重量由半磅改為三分之一磅，這項財政措施普遍被視為他最受非議的政策之一；五三三年貝利撒留的投射兵器有五百具發石機、五百具輕型弩砲與一百三十具投石機，全部由騾子牽引；六九八年羅馬軍在迦太基城下列出約五百七十具發石機與一百一十五具投石機。一具弩砲自重不過數十公斤，三人即可抬行，這是那些數字背後最小的、也是真正跟著部隊走的那一種器械。
dataEn: First, the chronology: the 511 of the card number falls at the turn of 511 and 512, which is where the revolt is usually dated. The chronicles place the seizure of Bononia in 512, the march on Ravenna in 513, the emperor's concessions and Vitalian's consulship between the end of 513 and the beginning of 514, and his murder on 28 December 515, or by some accounts 516; the Herulian drive into Italy after his death runs from 516 to 518. This entry takes 511 as the opening year, and the opening month can only be taken as the start of the year, because the documented beginnings of the revolt are the withholding of donatives and the gathering of old comrades, while the open seizure of a city falls in the following year. The geography of the campaign can be fixed by three points: Bologna, at 44.49 degrees north and 11.34 degrees east; Ravenna, at 44.42 degrees north and 12.20 degrees east; and Rome, at 41.53 degrees north and 12.30 degrees east. The road from Bologna to Ravenna is about two hundred and thirty kilometres and from Rome to Ravenna about three hundred. As for numbers, there are no exact figures to quote. Vitalian's rebel force was pieced together from the field armies of Illyricum and Pannonia and was probably in the range of several thousand to ten thousand men; the field army of the Roman Empire as a whole was very much larger, since the late Roman standing field establishment is listed at something like thirty limitanei legions, though the counts differ slightly from source to source, each of five hundred to a thousand men, and to these must be added cavalry and auxiliary troops, so that the overall total ran to tens of thousands. This shows that Vitalian's mutiny was nowhere near strong enough to match the empire's total strength; it succeeded because the emperor and the reserves were in the east while the decisive troops were in the north-west. A few sets of figures can be cited from the surrounding evidence: the number executed after the Akindynos affair differs from source to source and is given as several hundred; during his reign Anastasius reduced the weight of the gold solidus from half a libra to a third, and this financial measure is commonly held to be among the most disliked of his policies; in 533 Belisarius had five hundred mangonels, five hundred lighter bolt-throwers and a hundred thirty petraries, all drawn by mules; in 698 the Roman army before Carthage is credited with about five hundred seventy mangonels and a hundred fifteen petraries. A single bolt-thrower weighs no more than some tens of kilograms and can be carried by three men; it was the smallest of the machines, and the one that really travelled with the column.
cause: 起義的起因有兩層：近因是宮廷與軍隊之間的積怨，深因是皇帝在宗教與財政上的強行轉向。宗教上，阿納斯塔修斯是第一位把一性論傾向正式寫進帝國政策的皇帝，他在五一二年接連頒布法令，斥責反對一性論者為「三神論者」，並以國家力量支持君士坦丁堡的一性論教派；這在一個以卡爾西敦公會議為共識的帝國裡，等於把大批軍官與教士推到對立面。維塔利安打出的旗號正是維護卡爾西敦，軍中不少士兵因此響應，而東羅馬的邊軍既受教義爭論牽動，也受日耳曼部族與赫魯利人入侵的現實壓力，兩種不滿在同一支軍隊裡匯合。財政上，戰爭與邊防的開支不斷上升，帝國以提高稅額、調整金幣重量和拖延軍餉來維持平衡；軍隊的犒賞遲遲不發，士兵與家眷怨聲載道，這正是維塔利安在軍中一呼百應的土壤。阿金狄諾斯事件把宮廷清洗變成公開的恐怖：一位高官被皇帝親手處死，家屬被追，家產被抄，接著又借打著「冒名者」旗號的騷亂追殺數百人；這些數字背後是無數家庭被牽連的帝國菁英與軍官家庭。維塔利安反對的正是這個集團，他要求撤換克律薩菲烏斯，要求皇帝回到卡爾西敦，形式上是宗教綱領，實質上是一場以軍隊為後盾、要求更換執政者的政治罷工。外部條件同樣關鍵：赫魯利人和其他日耳曼部落正在多瑙河下游聚集，而帝國的注意力被東線吸住——五〇二至五〇三年與波斯王庫思德一世開戰，其後又忙於鎮壓首都的宗教騷動；西部邊軍的薪餉與徵召卻被放到最後一位。於是羅馬的邊軍在無人支持的情況下自己站出來，試圖用兵變去換一個換過人的朝廷。維塔利安提出的條件是要皇帝認錯、換人、改正宗教政策，這在一個以皇帝意志為秩序來源的帝國裡，等於要求執政者承認軍隊可以開條件。
causeEn: The revolt had two layers of cause: in the near term, the accumulated resentment between the court and the army; more deeply, the emperor's forced turn in religion and in finance. On religion, Anastasius was the first emperor to write the Monophysite tendency into imperial policy, and in 512 he issued a series of decrees condemning the opponents of the Monophysites as Trinitarians and backing the Monophysite party in Constantinople with the power of the state; in an empire where the Council of Chalcedon was the common ground, this put a great many officers and clerics on the other side. The banner Vitalian raised was precisely the defence of Chalcedon, and many soldiers answered it, while the eastern frontier troops were affected both by the doctrinal quarrel and by the practical pressure of the Germanic peoples and the Heruli, and the two discontents met in one and the same army. On finance, the cost of war and of the frontier kept rising, and the empire balanced its books by raising taxes, altering the weight of the coinage and delaying the soldiers' pay; the donatives did not arrive, and soldiers and their families talked openly about it, and that was the soil in which Vitalian's appeal took root. The Akindynos affair turned a purge in the palace into a public terror: a high official was put to death on the emperor's own order, his family was hunted and his property confiscated, and then a riot raised under the banner of an impostor was used as the pretext for the execution of several hundred more; behind those numbers lay the households of a great many of the empire's notables and military families. This was the group Vitalian was ranged against. His demands were the dismissal of Chrysaphius and a return to Chalcedon; in form a religious programme, in substance a political strike backed by the army and aimed at changing the men who governed. The external conditions mattered just as much: the Heruli and other Germanic peoples were gathering below the Danube, while the empire's attention was absorbed in the east, first by the war against the Persian king Kavad I in 502 and 503 and then by the suppression of religious disturbances in the capital; the pay and the recruitment of the western frontier came last in the queue. The western field army therefore stood up on its own, with nobody behind it, and tried to exchange a mutiny for a government that had been changed. What Vitalian demanded was that the emperor acknowledge his fault, dismiss the men around him and reverse his religious policy; in an empire whose whole order rested on the will of the emperor, that amounted to requiring the ruler to admit that the army was entitled to set terms.
impact: 維塔利安的起義在制度上的後果，比它在戰場上的成果更長久。第一，它開了羅馬晚期「軍人挾天子以令諸侯」的先例：皇帝為了換取一位叛軍將領的忠誠，交出執政官頭銜、讓出軍區指揮權、罷黜寵臣，五一五年甚至用暗殺的手段除掉這位自己冊封的功臣。皇位在後來一百年裡不斷被軍頭與禁軍首腦當作可以交易、可以廢立的籌碼，這條路的開端，正是維塔利安這幾年。第二，它把西部防線的崩解暴露在皇帝面前，也讓皇帝明白一性論政策在軍中的代價。五一八年阿納斯塔修斯病逝，其繼任者查士丁一世立刻轉向：五一九年與教宗霍爾米斯達斯（他本人支持卡爾西敦）達成和解，羅馬教會重新回到帝國的保護之下，教義問題的僵局由此解開，東西方關係的走向為之改觀，東哥特王狄多里克也在同一時期完成了對意大利的整合。第三，軍事上的直接後果是慘重的：赫魯利人西征，義大利的城市在戰火與饑饉中受損，羅馬在五一七年被圍，城市的糧道被切斷，守軍靠海上運糧勉強撐住，最後以談判和金錢換回被圍的羅馬人；義大利此後百餘年處於東哥特王國的統治之下，直到五三五年貝利撒留登陸才重新回到帝國版圖，而東哥特人收編殘餘羅馬軍與土地的長期政策也由此開端。第四，關於器械的記憶是間接的：這場戰爭本身沒有留下任何一件弩砲的記載，但它延續了一段羅馬投射兵器被大量用於野戰與圍城的傳統。晚羅馬的野戰軍在編制上仍保有投射兵器小隊，發石機與弩砲成為常備配備，這套配置在五三三年的義大利戰役與六九八年的迦太基之圍中達到可見的規模，並在拜占庭時代延續下來，正是在這些年份之後，希臘火藥與配重投石機的組合才逐漸改變了攻城戰的面貌。
impactEn: The institutional consequences of Vitalian's revolt outlasted its military results. First, it set the precedent by which, in the late empire, the army set terms with the emperor: to win the loyalty of a rebel commander, the emperor handed over a consulship, surrendered a regional command, dismissed a favourite, and in 515 even removed the man he had himself honoured, by assassination. For a century afterwards the throne was treated by generals and by the heads of the scholae as something that could be bargained over and deposed, and this episode is the beginning of that road. Second, it exposed the collapse of the western frontier to the emperor and taught him the price of the Monophysite policy in the army. Anastasius fell ill and died in 518, and his successor Justin I turned at once: in 519 he reached an accommodation with Pope Hormisdas, who himself supported Chalcedon, and the church of Rome came once more under imperial protection; the doctrinal deadlock was thereby broken and the course of relations between east and west changed, while Theodoric completed his consolidation of Italy in the same period. Third, the direct military consequences were heavy: the Herulian incursion left the cities of Italy damaged by war and by famine; Rome was besieged in 517 with its grain road cut off, the garrison held on only as long as seaborne grain kept coming, and the besieged Romans were finally bought back by negotiation and payment. Italy then remained in the hands of the Ostrogothic kingdom for more than a century, until the landing of Belisarius in 535 returned it to the empire, and the long Ostrogothic policy of absorbing the remaining Roman soldiers and the Roman land was launched from that moment. Fourth, the memory of the machine is indirect: this campaign itself leaves no trace of a single bolt-thrower, but it carried on a tradition in which Roman missile artillery was used heavily in the field and in siege. The late Roman field army still held missile units in its establishment, and mangonels and bolt-throwers became standard equipment, reaching a visible scale in the Italian campaigns of 533 and at the siege of Carthage in 698, and passing on into the Byzantine era, where it was after these same decades that the combination of Greek fire and counterweight trebuchets began to reshape the face of siege warfare.
result: 結局是起義的首領死了，起義的目標卻部分達成了。維塔利安在拉文納被姪子刺殺（史家或云皇帝授意，或云是其自身黨羽所為），史無明文可考；可以確定的是，他一死，依附他的將領在君士坦丁堡起事，帝國花了數年才把這些牽連收拾乾淨。他要求的撤換克律薩菲烏斯已在五一二至五一四年之間實現；要求皇帝回到卡爾西敦則要到他自己死後，由查士丁一世在五一九年完成。他留下的軍區與頭銜最終沒有傳給任何家族：色雷斯的軍權回到朝廷手上，重要的野戰軍指揮權在往後二十多年裡幾經轉手，落入貝利撒留與納爾塞斯一類人手中。義大利的戰局則走向另一個方向：赫魯利人與其他部落西征，義大利飽受兵禍；帝國在五一八年於波河平原擊潰入侵的日耳曼聯軍，俘獲的部眾被分派到帝國土地上的莊園屯墾，這一役之後西部邊境安定了數十年，直到狄多里克在五三〇年代入主義大利。就這場戰爭本身而言，可以確定的事實是：維塔利安以伊利利亞的一支野戰軍起事，控制了潘諾尼亞與達爾馬提亞，把北意大利的通道切斷數年，逼得皇帝連讓三步——換掉寵臣、准他進軍首都、給他執政官與軍區總督的頭銜；而他以為這是交易的開始，最後卻成了交易的終點。以軍隊的實力向皇帝開價，在五世紀的羅馬只成功過這一次；它也正因如此，成了後世軍人政治的反覆引例。關於卡面這件羅馬弩砲，只能說明它所在的位置：它是這支部隊在行軍途中必然帶著的投射兵器，架在營門與側翼，射擊逼近的密集隊形，攻城時用來壓制城頭；而拉文納的圍城結局並不是由任何器械決定的，是由糧道、談判與一次暗殺決定的。史書在這裡保持沉默，而這份沉默本身就是這場戰爭的寫照。
resultEn: The outcome was that the leader of the revolt died while part of its purpose was achieved. Vitalian was killed by his nephew at Ravenna; whether the emperor had sanctioned it or it was done by his own partisans is not settled by the written record. What is certain is that his death was followed by a rising of his adherents in Constantinople, and the empire needed several years to clean up the consequences. The dismissal of Chrysaphius that he had demanded was carried out between 512 and 514; the return to Chalcedon he had demanded was achieved only after his own death, by Justin I in 519. The commands and the titles he had obtained passed to no family: the Thracian command returned to the court, and the key field commands of the army changed hands several times in the following quarter century before falling to men of the stamp of Belisarius and Narses. The Italian situation ran in another direction: the Heruli and the other peoples came west, Italy suffered heavily from the war, and in 518 the imperial army destroyed the invading Germanic confederation in the plain of the Po, after which the captives were distributed among the estates of imperial territory as settlers, and the western frontier was quiet for several decades until Theodoric entered Italy in the 530s. As for this campaign itself, the facts that can be established are these: Vitalian rose with a single Illyrian field army, held Pannonia and Dalmatia, cut the communications of northern Italy for several years, and forced the emperor into three consecutive concessions, the dismissal of the favourite, permission to enter Rome in triumph, and the consulship together with a regional command; and he believed this was the beginning of a bargain, when it was in fact the end of it. Making terms with the emperor backed by an army succeeded in fifth-century Rome only once, and precisely for that reason it became the standing example quoted in every later account of military politics. As for the Roman scorpio on the card, only its place can be stated: it was the missile engine the column necessarily carried on the march, set up at the camp gates and on the flanks, firing into approaching formations and used against the walls in siege, while the outcome of the siege of Ravenna was decided by no machine at all but by the grain road, by negotiation and by an assassination. The chroniclers are silent on the point, and that silence is itself the portrait of this war.
